current.text: Portland has a new head coach this season.
Portland added Ja Morant and Damian Lillard, and Scoot Henderson returns for a full season. All three are on-ball point guards.
Morant, Lillard and Henderson played about 15 games combined last season.
The backcourt is crowded. Lillard, Morant, Jrue Holiday, Deni Avdija, Henderson and Shaedon Sharpe all share the ball and the playmaking.
Portland has too many high-usage guards (Lillard, Morant, Henderson, Avdija). Their combined numbers from last season cannot all hold.
The added guards cut Deni Avdija's usage and passing and squeeze his on-ball role.
The crowded guard group adds risk to Damian Lillard.
The projected starting five is Lillard, Morant, Toumani Camara, Avdija and Donovan Clingan.
Holiday, Henderson and Sharpe are expected to come off the bench.
Lillard and Morant are expected to be staggered, but both should close games.
Forward depth is very thin. Avdija and Camara are basically the only forwards. Portland lost Jerami Grant, Matisse Thybulle, Kris Murray, Caleb Love and Blake Wesley.
Portland added several centers. Clingan starts, and Yang Hansen and Robert Williams III are also in the center group.
Mike Richman of Locked On Blazers does not expect Clingan to play over 28 minutes.
The team wants bigs who stay out of the paint so Avdija and Morant can drive downhill.
Portland's guards should convert fewer passes into assists because Camara, Clingan and Avdija are poor finishers.
Minutes and usage should swing from game to game across the rotation.
The Lillard and Morant backcourt is undersized and poor on defense. Transition defense is projected to be poor, and offensive rebounding got worse.
Portland projects as a middle team with about 44 wins (range 40 to 45). It should be a playoff or play-in team.
Portland was rumored in a trade for Jaylen Brown. That deal would likely send out Henderson or another guard.
A consolidation trade to fix the guard glut is doubted.
Portland has a back-to-back in each fantasy playoff week, three in total. That adds rest risk when it matters most.
Portland has a five-game week starting February 8.

note: Portland has too many high-usage guards (Lillard, Morant, Henderson, Holiday, Avdija) under a new coach. Expect every guard's usage and assists to come down, with game-to-game swings, and Avdija loses the most of his on-ball role. Clingan should be capped near 28 minutes. In the first weeks, watch who closes games, how the bench guard minutes split, and any trade that clears the guard glut.
